title: Planning-oriented Autonomous Driving
grouping: Left column holds (a) standalone models and (b) a multi-task framework; a thin vertical grey rule separates it from (c), which stacks three rows (c.1 vanilla, c.2 explicit design, c.3 the proposed design). An italic grey axis 'perception - prediction - planning' runs under (c) as a phase scale.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles: grey filled task boxes, white outlined modules and heads, small node-link networks for the standalone models, a grey 3-D feature-stack glyph for each backbone. Each row in (c) starts with the same backbone glyph and ends with a red 'Planner' box (dashed outline in c.2). In c.3 the module boxes take the overview's colours (blue tracking, purple mapping, green motion, yellow occupancy, red planner). Sans-serif labels.
proposed_highlight: The proposed row is the only coloured one, its sub-caption is bold and ends with '(Ours)', and its module colours match the main overview figure.
lesson: Compare driving paradigms as stacked rows that share the same backbone glyph at the left and the same red Planner box at the right, so only the middle changes; colour only the proposed row, in the overview's module colours.
notes: Venue CVPR 2023 from the arXiv comment (venue_source: arxiv-journal-ref). The whole figure is a single raster image in the PDF (refs crop recorded one embedded image covering the crop), so kb measure cannot separate photos from drawing: photo_share is null and the palette includes the embedded photos and renders. Annotation note (2026-11-15): teaser/paradigm-comparison figure, not the method pipeline (that is fig 2)

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: driving paradigms drawn as stacked rows that each start from the same grey backbone-slab glyph, with (c.1)-(c.3) sharing a planner box at the right end so only the middle of each row changes; the proposed row c.3 is last and the only coloured one

relations.form: (a) standalone models and (b) multi-task framework stacked in a narrow left column, separated by a vertical rule from (c) end-to-end driving, whose three rows c.1 vanilla, c.2 explicit, c.3 planning-oriented (Ours) stack top to bottom
within c.3 Tracking and Mapping on two short branches feed Motion -> Occupancy -> Planner left to right
an italic 'perception - prediction - planning' scale on a thin rule under (c) aligns the columns of c.3 with its stages
Tracking and Mapping converge on Motion, and a bypass line from Motion skips Occupancy into Planner

channels.colour: only the proposed row is coloured, one hue per task (blue tracking, purple mapping, green motion, yellow occupancy, red planner); the planner is also red in c.1, so red marks the planning target in rows that reach it while grey/white mark prior designs
channels.shape: grey stacked slabs are backbone features, small node-link graphs are standalone networks in (a), rounded boxes are tasks/modules
channels.line: solid arrows are data flow; c.2's last arrow is dotted into a dashed-outline planner, marking a weak or missing connection
channels.frame: no frames; panels are separated by whitespace, captions and one vertical rule

quality.strengths: Rows share their left and right anchors so the reader compares only the middle; ours is last and the only saturated row; the stage scale under (c) ties the proposed chain to perception/prediction/planning; module colours match the paper's overview figure.
quality.weaknesses: Red planner appears in c.1 as well as ours, so red does not uniquely mean 'ours'; panels (a) and (b) are squeezed into a narrow column at a different scale from (c); no data or outputs are shown, so the paradigms differ only in box topology.

insights.structure: Three captioned panels: (a) standalone models and (b) multi-task framework stacked in the narrow left column, and (c) end-to-end driving filling the right two-thirds as three stacked rows c.1 vanilla, c.2 explicit design, c.3 planning-oriented design (ours), separated by a vertical rule.
insights.data: Inputs are small grey 3-D feature-slab glyphs on the left of each row, neural nets in (a) are drawn as tiny node-link graphs, and tasks are grey rounded boxes; no real data is shown.
insights.emphasis: Only row c.3 uses colour (blue Tracking, purple Mapping, green Motion, yellow Occupancy, red Planner) and a bold caption '(Ours)', while the alternatives are grey or white; the Planner target is red in c.1 and c.3 but a dashed outline in c.2.
insights.flow: Each row reads left to right from backbone glyph to task; along the bottom of (c) the italic stage words perception - prediction - planning on a thin rule align the columns of c.3.
insights.avoid: This is a teaser comparing design paradigms rather than the method architecture; the grey-on-white alternatives leave lots of empty space in c.1.

arrangement.units: three captioned panels (a), (b), (c) split by a thin vertical rule; (c) holds three unframed rows c.1-c.3 each with its own caption on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: grey feature-slab glyphs or node-link model icons at the left of every row
